steps.body: Scan the ones digits before you start: two addends whose ones make a ten are a friendly pair — add them first and bank a clean ten.
steps.narration: Scan the ones digits before you start: two addends whose ones make a ten are a friendly pair — add them first and bank a clean ten.

widget.prompt: Tap the TWO addends whose ones make a ten: 38, 25, 12.

hotspots.feedback: 25 has 5 ones — with 8 that makes 13, missing the clean ten that 8 + 2 delivers.

widget.missFeedback: Look at the ONES digits — the friendly pair is the one whose ones complete a ten.
widget.successFeedback: That pair's ones complete a ten — banking it first makes the rest easy.

predict.prompt: In 38 + 25 + 12, which pair lands on a ten?
predict.reveal: 8 ones + 2 ones = 10, so 38 + 12 = 50 exactly — the middle addend waits its turn.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2n find tens.
invariants: Regrouping addends changes the ORDER of joining, never the total — every staging of the sum must land on the same number for g2n find tens.
misconceptions: Believing the grouping or order of addends can change a sum, or letting an addend join twice or not at all while restaging.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Which single change to the staging would actually change the total — and which only changes the path?

explanationVariants: The chosen ones complete a ten.

commonErrors.feedback: A make-ten pair lands exactly on a ten — no leftover ones at all.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Stage the sum: pick a pair, bank the total, and let each remaining addend join one at a time.

widget.prompt: In 26 + 14 + 24, which two addends make the friendliest pair to add FIRST?

options.label: 26 and 24 — their ones make a ten
options.feedback: Correct — 6 + 4 = 10, so 26 + 24 lands on a clean ten and the rest joins easily.

options.label: 26 and 14 — they come first
options.feedback: Order on the page is not a strategy; their ones (6 + 4) miss the ten.

options.label: 14 and 24 — the biggest two
options.feedback: Size alone does not help; those ones (4 + 4) do not complete a ten.

options.label: 26 and 15 — they look alike
options.feedback: 15 is not even in this sum — a pair must come from the addends you actually have.
